title: AI And The New Problem with Processes And Support
author: bingewavecinema
selftext:
My game has missed it launched and Steam has not responded in weeks. Which sucks because I can't communicate nor coordinate with anyone else; influencers, wishlisters, media, no one because I can't get any kind of response. I can't even change my launch date.

And I was growing at about 100+ wishlist a day, and now that momentum is lost

I get they are swamped but it really unprofessional for them not respond at all.

And I want to make this clear; just because it AI doesn't mean its slop. There have been plenty of games that have sold, made money and people have enjoyed that are not slop but made with AI. So banning games with AI is not the solution.

The real problem that AI has created is the processes haven't caught up to the output from AI and the amount of low effort slop that becomes generated.

I think what Valve in making people test their games and take screenshots is partly the remove move; I also think it can use numerical data as well to create a queue. Meaning no wishlist, no players, then back of the queue. A hot growing game, should go in front of the queue. This way it doesn't negatively effect games that had effort put into them and are likely to sell.
